text:
Michael Brandsegg-Nygård has played 24 games for Detroit and thrown 111 hits, which tells you how he has earned a regular spot at 21. The 2024 first-rounder from Oslo, 15th overall, came over from the SHL with one point in 14 NHL games last season and has 12 in 24 this season, a pace ahead of the median first full season for forwards picked around him (0.35 points a game).

The finishing hasn't followed the chances. He has 4 goals on 7.5 expected, and his 1.22 expected goals per 60 on his own shots is more than double last season's. He also owns one of the hardest shots in the league, 98th percentile in top speed by the NHL's EDGE tracking. Goals tend to follow looks like that.

Detroit's November has been grim, with seven losses in eight games before Wednesday's win over Vancouver, but the Red Wings have been on the right side of the shot share with him on the ice (55% of attempts at five on five). Evolving-Hockey's small 2025-26 sample liked his defense (87th percentile at limiting chances against).

He's a bottom-six grinder with a shooter's tools. The goals are behind; the rest looks real.
headline: Brandsegg-Nygård hits everything, scores less
